_label: FAKE keys, self-consistent — NOT captured from real NTAG 424 DNA silicon.
_warning: Every `cmac` below was produced by Tappa's OWN pipeline (sv2 + RFC-4493 cmac + truncateSDMMAC in internal/sun) keyed by the FAKE test keys in this file. All key material here is FAKE (never a real per-tag K_sdmfileread, never the real TAPPA_TAG_KEK); real keys are random (ADR 0003 madde 3) and live only KEK-wrapped in the DB.

WHAT THESE PROVE: the Verify wiring end to end — resolve, retired/lost short-circuit, QR short-circuit, KEK unwrap, truncated-CMAC compare, the verify-BEFORE-advance order, monotonic replay ordering (accept / replay / backward / forward-gap), and the reject paths (wrong key, bit flip, malformed input, unknown uid). They pin the internal layout against regressions.

WHAT THEY DO NOT PROVE (self-consistency ceiling): because the same code both mints and checks these MACs, a defect present in that code is present on BOTH sides of every comparison here and stays invisible. THIS IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL — it is what happened. From M2-04 until M2-08 (2026-08-18) sv2() appended the read counter in the WRONG BYTE ORDER, every vector in this file was minted with that defect, and the whole suite was green. A real chip's first 255 taps would all have been rejected.

⚠️ THE CEILING IS NOW LOWER, BUT IT IS STILL THERE. M2-08 added EXTERNALLY SOURCED known-answer vectors in internal/sun/an12196_kat_test.go, transcribed from NXP AN12196's published worked examples (rev. 1.8 §4.3 Table 2 p.10 -- rev. 2.0 renumbers it Table 1, p.9 -- and rev. 1.8 §4.4.4.2.1 Table 5 p.15). Those DO externally anchor the SV2 byte layout, the session-key derivation, the empty MAC input and the odd-indexed truncation — the chain this file cannot anchor. The AES-CMAC primitive under it is anchored separately by the official RFC 4493 vectors in cmac_test.go.

⚠️ ONE ANCHOR, NOT TWO, ON THE URL BYTE-ORDER AXIS (section and table numbers below are rev. 1.8's). Read the previous bullet narrowly: the counter's URL spelling rests ONLY on Table 2's SV2 counter 010000 read against §4.4.1's plain URL ctr=000001 for the same UID. Table 5 does NOT independently re-pin it — Table 5 is the ENCRYPTED-PICCData example, its UID and counter come out of decrypting PICCENCData (step 3), and the URL published for it (§4.4.2.1) carries ?e=...&c=... with no plain ctr= at all. The MSB-first URL counter used in that test (00003D) appears NOWHERE in either revision as laid out: it is Tappa's derivation. (A whitespace-collapsed search shows one apparent hit in rev 2.0; that is two table cells joined -- the all-zero key's trailing 0000 plus the next row's step number 3 and D( -- not an occurrence.) What Table 5 adds is that sv2() really reverses (3D0000 is non-palindromic), which is a property of our code, not a second reading of the wire.

WHAT REMAINS UNPROVEN AFTER M2-08: no physical NTAG 424 DNA has been read. AN12196 anchors our DECODE side to NXP's description of the chip; it cannot prove our ENCODE side (M8-05 runbook) mirrors the counter into the URL MSB-first, which ADR 0003 §1 decides and the vectors assume. A real-chip capture is still wanted before the M8 pilot. Do NOT read a green run of THIS file as proof of real-chip correctness.

The counter VALUE endianness (Params.Ctr, big-endian per ADR 0003 §1) is no longer a separate open axis: AN12196 §4.4.1 (p.11) publishes the plain URL `ctr=000001` for the same UID whose SDMReadCtr §4.3 Table 2 gives as `010000 (LSB first)`, so the URL is MSB-first and SV2 is LSB-first — one value, two spellings, reversed exactly once in sv2(). See verify_mac_test.go TestSV2_CounterIsReversedIntoLSBFirstOrder and the KAT file above.
_regenerate: HOW TO REGENERATE THE `cmac` FIELDS BELOW (last done: M2-08, 2026-08-18, after the sv2 byte-order fix).

Regenerate ONLY when the algorithm intentionally changes. If these go red without an intended change, the CODE is wrong — do not refresh the values to make the suite green. Check an12196_kat_test.go first: if the external KATs are also red, the chain broke; if only this file is red, the fixture is stale.

The recipe below uses openssl, deliberately NOT the Go code under test, so regenerating is a second implementation rather than a copy of the first. Chain: SV2 = 3CC300010080 || UID || reverse(ctr_hex); K_ses = AES-CMAC(tag_key, SV2); full = AES-CMAC(K_ses, <empty>); cmac = odd-indexed bytes 1,3,5,7,9,11,13,15 of full.

🔴 NEVER RUN THIS RECIPE WITH A REAL PLAQUE KEY — NOT ONCE, NOT 'just to check a tap'. It puts the key on the COMMAND LINE (`openssl mac ... hexkey:"$1"`), where every process on the box can read it out of `ps`, and it lands in the shell history file. That is safe here only because every key in this file is FAKE (CLAUDE.md §4.7). The shape is the danger: the day someone wants to hand-verify a real tag's MAC, this is the ready-made tool sitting in their editor, and using it leaks a per-tag K_sdmfileread that lives KEK-wrapped everywhere else. If you need to verify a real plaque, do it in a process that reads the key from a file or the environment and never as an argv element — the operator rules in deploy/README.md ('Anahtar hijyeni — iddia değil, mekanizma', and the KEK rotation section's argv/xtrace refusals) already state the same rule for the KEK and are the reference for how it is done.

cm() { if [ -z "$2" ]; then printf '' | openssl mac -macopt cipher:AES-128-CBC -macopt hexkey:"$1" CMAC; else printf '%s' "$2" | xxd -r -p | openssl mac -macopt cipher:AES-128-CBC -macopt hexkey:"$1" CMAC; fi | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z'; }

Then per vector: sdmmac <tag_key> <uid> <ctr_hex>. The `wrong_key` row is minted with tag_key_B_wrong (so it must NOT verify against tag_key_A), and `single_bit_flip` is a valid MAC for its row with the LOW BIT OF BYTE 0 flipped. Verify with: go test -run 'TestVerify_VectorsSelfConsistent|TestSDMKAT_' ./internal/sun/
The `malformed` queries carry a cmac only so the string is well-formed; their values are never verified, but they are kept consistent with valid_consecutive so no stale value looks meaningful.

vectors.name: valid_consecutive
vectors.description: valid CMAC, ctr = last_ctr + 1 -> accept, last_ctr updated, gap 0

vectors.name: replay_equal
vectors.description: valid CMAC, ctr = last_ctr -> reject (replay), last_ctr unchanged

vectors.name: backward_counter
vectors.description: valid CMAC, ctr < last_ctr -> reject (backward counter), last_ctr unchanged

vectors.name: forward_jump_5000
vectors.description: valid CMAC, ctr = last_ctr + 5000 -> accept, gap 4999 returned (threshold is policy, not sun)

vectors.name: wrong_key
vectors.description: CMAC minted with tag_key_B but tag holds tag_key_A -> reject, no advance

vectors.name: single_bit_flip
vectors.description: valid CMAC with one bit flipped (09fa... -> 08fa...) -> reject, no advance
